video_title: Denver Nuggets Full Practice Media Availability | 10.18.26

quotes.speaker: Spencer Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Spencer Jones on the impact of new defensive concepts
quotes.excerpt: we're changing significant defensive concepts, especially because the whole second unit's new
quotes.quote: It's been annoying, been a lot of film, especially because we're changing significant defensive concepts, especially because the whole second unit's new and stuff like that. So you want to get that chemistry and stuff like that. So that's been annoying and stuff like that. But like I said, you own up to it by doing extra film sessions, talking to coaches, and just paying attention to see how guys are working, and certain guys' spots in the second unit to know how you would work out of them.
quotes.social_post: Spencer Jones says the Nuggets are implementing significant new defensive concepts this season. He admits the process has been annoying but notes the team is putting in extra film work to build chemistry with the new second unit.

quotes.speaker: Spencer Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Spencer Jones on the Nuggets' offensive identity
quotes.excerpt: last year the offensive focus was definitely pick and roll with Jamal, getting him in the post
quotes.quote: Last year the offensive focus was definitely pick and roll with Jamal, getting him in the post, and then Tim Hardaway trying to get him as many shots, and then playing off of that, how the defense reacts to that. This year, it's definitely still that pick and roll concept with Trevon Brazile really being a great passer and facilitator, which gets everyone involved, which I think that's amazing. And having a mid-post hub like Nikola Jokic, at least for me especially, keeps it pretty consistent with how I play with Nikola, in terms of who we're looking for in the end of the possession.
quotes.social_post: Spencer Jones says the Nuggets offense is shifting toward a pick and roll focus with Trevon Brazile as a primary facilitator. He notes that having a mid post hub like Nikola Jokic keeps the offensive flow consistent for him.

quotes.speaker: Spencer Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Spencer Jones on playing with Trevon Brazile
quotes.excerpt: Trevon Brazile in terms of he's looking at me in the corners a lot
quotes.quote: Trevon Brazile in terms of he's looking at me in the corners a lot, and so I know I'll be getting a bit more volume for threes and just knowing that he's constantly looking for us on cuts as he's coming off screens and everything like that. You know he's more of a pass-first guy, that'll be that'll be amazing. Like I said, Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic being able to play out of a hub out of him, and then just like how how much we're going to move the ball, maybe a bit more than the first unit just because like look, you got Jamal and Nikola, you want the ball in their hands.
quotes.social_post: Spencer Jones expects more volume from the corner this season playing alongside Trevon Brazile. He describes Brazile as a pass first player who is constantly looking for shooters and cutters.

quotes.speaker: Trevon Brazile
quotes.summary_phrase: Trevon Brazile on learning to play with Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray
quotes.excerpt: the main thing, playing with Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, was seeing the ball earlier
quotes.quote: I made a lot of mistakes, I knew I was going to go in just trying to go in and play hard. But I would say the main thing, playing with Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, was seeing the ball earlier, especially in transition. That was kind of my first time in a game setting with them, so just getting adjusted to that.
quotes.social_post: Trevon Brazile says his biggest adjustment playing with Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray is learning to see the ball earlier in transition. He admits he made mistakes but is focused on playing hard.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Trevon Brazile's development
quotes.excerpt: he's got to learn to find the ball earlier offensively. Getting on the rim is one thing
quotes.quote: He's got to learn to find the ball earlier offensively. Getting on the rim is one thing, seeing the ball as you do it is another. That attracts people to you, but he did a lot of good things. I'm just happy to see him confidently shoot the ball and look comfortable doing it in a real NBA game.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman says Trevon Brazile needs to improve at finding the ball earlier on offense. He was encouraged by Brazile's confidence shooting the ball in a real NBA game setting.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on rotation plans for the season
quotes.excerpt: we have the week to go and I think the first two games will keep the group together
quotes.quote: We haven't decided that yet. We have the week to go and I think the first two games will keep the group together, as a, you know, because I think we're still looking at it. Are we playing a nine-man rotation, 10-man rotation, and then like I said, kind of a fake 11-man rotation where if the first half doesn't work out, is there somebody that you say, why don't we change it up and play them in the third quarter? A small amount of minutes, but just rotate them in. I think that's where we're at. All those guys, Trevon Brazile's obviously been more of a highlight thing, he's played really well. He also has played the most minutes with the best players, but I think Bryce has shown signs, Cam Whitmore shown signs, so you can't be scared to throw those guys out there as we're looking for a rotation.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman says the Nuggets are still deciding on their rotation size. He is considering a 9 or 10 man rotation with the possibility of an 11th man getting spot minutes if the first half does not go as planned.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Spencer Jones's defensive value
quotes.excerpt: defensively, it's enormous because you're switching somebody onto the ball that can really guard
quotes.quote: Defensively, it's enormous because you're switching somebody onto the ball that can really guard, and then if he switches off the ball, he can really rebound, keep people off the glass, high intelligence. And then on the flip side, the way they guard, how aggressive they are with our main two people, you have to make threes to beat them. The way they shrink the paint, and guys like Spencer Jones that can have a big night and get hot, you know obviously that goes a long way against that team.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman praises Spencer Jones for his defensive versatility and high IQ. He notes that Jones is a crucial floor spacer who can get hot and help the team beat defenses that shrink the paint.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Spencer Jones's role
quotes.excerpt: I think it was tough for him in a way today because we flowed him back in
quotes.quote: I actually thought it was tough for him in a way today because we flowed him back in as more of a three-man, just to try to keep a five-man group out there with no starter. Spencer is obviously very high IQ, he can fill in and play different spots. But it was weird to come back for the first time the guy starting in the playoffs as a four and we're like, hey, go play three today. But no, I thought for Spencer it was unfortunate. I mean he's such a, he's a connector when he plays, he just does the right thing, so I'm just glad he's back out on the court.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman calls Spencer Jones a connector who always does the right thing. He noted it was a tough transition for Jones to move from a playoff starter at the four to playing the three in practice today.
